The given equation is \((x-1) \cdot f(x) = 3x^4 + x^3 - 25x^2 + 38x - 17\). Since \(f\) is stated to be a polynomial, the right-hand side must be divisible by \(x-1\). We can verify this by evaluating the right-hand side at \(x = 1\):

\[
3(1)^4 + (1)^3 - 25(1)^2 + 38(1) - 17 = 3 + 1 - 25 + 38 - 17 = 0.
\]

Indeed, \(x=1\) is a root, so divisibility holds. The degree of the product \((x-1) \cdot f(x)\) is the degree of \(x-1\) (which is 1) plus the degree of \(f(x)\), assuming \(f\) is nonzero. The right-hand side is a polynomial of degree 4. Therefore, \(\deg(f) + 1 = 4\), which gives \(\deg(f) = 3\). (Performing the division yields \(f(x) = 3x^3 + 4x^2 - 21x + 17\), confirming the degree is 3.)

Answer: 3
